newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS sales down 8 pct due to boycott-agency.
newsitem.headline: SAS sales down 8 pct due to boycott-agency.

text.p: Denmark's leading business travel agency estimated on Tuesday that sales of Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) tickets were down eight percent due to a protest boycott by Nordic business travel specialists.

"From January 2-17 our SAS sales were four percent down on the same time last year. The boycott was only in effect for half the period," Ole Andersen, managing director at Carlson Wagon Lit Travel, Denmark's top business travel agency told Reuters.
"This leads me to calculate that sales have fallen by around eight percent. We had expected a drop of between five and 10 percent in SAS ticket sales so the figure fits," he said.
Andersen said that Danish travel bureaux sold some two billion crowns worth of SAS tickets annually, estimating that the boycott had caused the airline some 160 million crowns in losses so far.

Danish members of the Guild of European Business Travel Agents said on January 10 that they would book clients with competitors to SAS wherever possible in protest against a 50 percent cut in agents' commissions imposed by the carrier.
Travel agents in Norway and Sweden are also participating in the action.
In Norway losses in revenue to SAS due to the boycott are put at around 10 million Norwegian crowns for the first two weeks of January.
On Monday SAS said it had no plans to revoke the cut.
A meeting between the carrier and Nordic travel agents is scheduled to discuss the issue in Stockholm on Wednesday.
SAS argues that technological advances, such as ticketless travel and annual passes, have greatly reduced the effort required from agents.
